We're doing baked beans with (smoked) pulled pork sandwiches. The pulled pork is actually from a few months ago, we had a TON of leftover so it went into a vacuum bag and into the freezer. But, I made the baked beans from scratch starting with the overnight soak of some Great Northerns: Baked Beans

Ingredients

 1 lb dried navy beans, picked over and rinsed (about 2 cups)
 6 thick-sliced bacon, cut into 1/2-inch squares
 1 onion, chopped fine
 5 cups water
 5 tablespoons dark brown sugar, packed
 1/4 cup molasses
 2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce
 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
 2 teaspoons cider vinegar
 salt and pepper
 1 tablespoon molasses
 1 teaspoons Dijon mustard

Instructions

 Cook bacon in pot over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 10 minutes. 
 Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. 
 Stir in water, beans, sugar, 1/4 cup molasses, Worcestershire, 1 tablespoon mustard, vinegar, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper and bring to boil. 
 Cover and cook until beans are nearly tender, about 2 1/2 hours.
 
 Optional: slow cooker on high for 7 hours
 
 Stir in remaining 1 tablespoon molasses and remaining 1 teaspoon mustard. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve. 

(Beans can be refrigerated for up to 4 days.).

This is a Hodge-podge recipe, I started with a Cooks Country/America's Test Kitchen/Cooks Illustrated recipe, Here, but could never get it to turn out right. I combined it with Another recipe that didn't taste nearly as good but I turned out well every time to form the above. When doing the stove-top method, the beans don't soak up the color so it looks a little odd, but I guarantee that the taste is right on the money (at least for my pallet).
